transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lara, Tom, Priya (Meridian)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, optional): quick hosted API demo showing embeddings + reranking endpoints; discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, prefix caching, embedding refresh cadence; agreed on pilot deliverables.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Ethan, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:06] Lara Gomez: Good thanks, Maya. Excited to see the sandbox. We want to focus on improving search relevance across product docs and support tickets.
[00:00:12] Ethan Cole: Great, we'll walk through the hosted embeddings endpoint and the reranking flow. Quick note — parts of this demo are running in our hosted sandbox and some perf numbers are approximated for demo data.
[00:00:21] Tom Ibrahim: Sounds good. Our constraints: sub-200ms 99p on search queries and we want to avoid bringing everything in-house for now. Also we have a rolling embedding refresh every 24 hours.
[00:00:32] Priya Reddy: And our infra folks care about VPC options and KMS key integration, but for the pilot hosted is preferred.
[00:00:38] Maya Patel: Perfect, that's aligned with most pilots. We'll show how hosted API can meet latency targets and where dedicated or private would fit later. Ethan: take it away.
[00:00:45] Ethan Cole: Cool. Starting screen share — I'm on the Redwood Console demo org. First slide — the embeddings endpoint. You can see a simple POST to /v1/embeddings, payload with text or batch of texts. For bulk loads we recommend the batch API with chunking.
[00:01:02] Ethan Cole: (mumble) the model we typically use for dense vectors is the redwood-embed-small for cost sensitive workloads, or redwood-embed-large for higher recall. Note: model names sometimes appear in the transcript as "redwood embed" or "reed wood" — apologies if the transcription mangles that.
[00:01:18] Lara Gomez: Quick question — any recommended dimensionality? We're currently on a 512 float vector from our older pipeline.
[00:01:24] Ethan Cole: Good question. 384-512 is a common sweet spot; our small model outputs 384, large 768. For your 10k doc corpus 384 should be OK, reduces storage and speeds ANN.
[00:01:36] Tom Ibrahim: How do you handle embedding refreshes? We want incremental updates rather than re-embedding the whole index every day.
[00:01:41] Ethan Cole: We recommend incremental refresh — send diffs to the embedding endpoint and update vector store. Also can use our webhook hooks or a small scheduler to do partial refresh windows so you're under quotas. We'll share an example runbook.
[00:01:54] Priya Reddy: Do you have a managed vector store or do we bring our own?
[00:01:58] Maya Patel: We integrate with common vector DBs like Pinecone, Milvus, and also self-hosting if desired. For pilots many customers use Pinecone or our recommended open-source store in the sample repo.
[00:02:07] Lara Gomez: OK. Next?
[00:02:10] Ethan Cole: Moving to reranking. High-level: first pass retrieval via ANN, then call Redwood's reranker endpoint with the query plus N candidates. The reranker returns a score and optionally a structured explanation. In the Console demo you'll see an API call pattern: /v1/rerank with inputs: query, candidates (ids + snippets).
[00:02:29] Ethan Cole: The reranker is optimized for latency; for hosted we tune batch size and max context to keep tail latency low. In practice we see rerank 5-10 candidates under 120-180ms on standard configs.
[00:02:41] Tom Ibrahim: 120-180ms on rerank — is that additional to ANN lookup? So total is lookup plus rerank?
[00:02:45] Ethan Cole: Correct, but lookup is typically sub-50ms depending on vector DB. So you could be in the 170-230ms range end-to-end; if you need consistent sub-200ms 99p we can discuss Dedicated lanes or prefix caching to shave tail.
[00:02:58] Lara Gomez: That tail is our worry. We have spikes from long queries and long contexts. What about KV cache?
[00:03:05] Ethan Cole: We have prefix/KV caching for generative flows; for rerank we use request-level caching for frequent queries and also support small LRU caches at the application layer. Also you can pin popular items to skip rerank if they match exact signals.
[00:03:20] Priya Reddy: On security, can you walk through KMS and audit logs for hosted pilots?
[00:03:25] Maya Patel: Sure. Hosted supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption at rest; audit logs are available via the Console exports and can be streamed to your SIEM. For regulated workloads, our Private product runs in a VPC with isolated control plane and HSM options.
[00:03:40] Tom Ibrahim: Do you have SOC 2 or ISO certs?
[00:03:43] Maya Patel: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II; I'll share the compliance pack after the call.
[00:03:48] Lara Gomez: Great. Back to relevance: can we see a live example with our sample doc set?
[00:03:52] Ethan Cole: I pulled in a small 500-doc sample for the demo. I'm going to run the retrieval+rerank flow now.
[00:03:57] [00:04:00] Ethan Cole: (typing noises) First, hitting embeddings API with a batch — you can see the returned vectors. Then the ANN search — returning 50 candidates in 22ms. Now posting to rerank with top 10 snippets.
[00:04:16] Ethan Cole: Result — reranker scores and final ordering. You can see a sample structured output: label, score, rationale — this helps downstream for explainability.
[00:04:26] Lara Gomez: That rationale looks useful. Is that deterministic? Sometimes our current reranker gives inconsistent reasons.
[00:04:31] Ethan Cole: Rationale can vary slightly between model versions; we recommend pinning model versions in the Console for production. The Console shows model catalog, performance profiles, and rollout controls.
[00:04:41] Priya Reddy: Rollouts — can we do canary for reranker only?
[00:04:44] Maya Patel: Yes, you can do per-route rollouts: canary X% traffic to new reranker model, automatic fallback if regressions detected by evals. "Optimize" module can suggest configuration changes based on cost/quality tradeoffs.
[00:04:57] Tom Ibrahim: Speaking of cost, give me a sense of token vs embedding cost. We currently run many small queries.
[00:05:03] Maya Patel: Embeddings are billed per vector unit and rerank per request. For high-query volume, you can use smaller embed models and cache, or compress vectors. I'll include pricing examples in the email.
[00:05:12] Lara Gomez: Any guidance on number of candidates to rerank? We're guessing 100 is overkill.
[00:05:18] Ethan Cole: Exactly — 5-20 candidates is typical. You trade compute for recall: 10 is common starting point, then profile. Our Optimize tool can run evals on your labeled set and recommend candidate counts and model variants.
[00:05:31] [00:05:35] (brief crosstalk)
[00:05:40] Priya Reddy: For pilot SLA what do you need from us?
[00:05:43] Maya Patel: A 10k doc sample, a list of high-frequency queries, and success metrics (e.g., NDCG or mean reciprocal rank targets). We'll provision a sandbox project and share API keys scoped to pilot.
[00:05:55] Lara Gomez: We'll provide the sample and baseline metrics by Friday. Can you show how we wire this into our search stack?
[00:06:02] Ethan Cole: Sure — here's a simplified diagram: ingest -> embeddings -> vector store -> ANN candidate set -> rerank via Redwood endpoint -> final results. For existing pipelines you mostly drop in the embedding call and the rerank API, minimal changes. I have a small code example in Node and Python in the repo.
[00:06:20] Tom Ibrahim: Any network constraints? We run in us-east and prefer low egress.
[00:06:24] Maya Patel: Our hosted regions include us-east and eu-west; for low-egress you can use region pinning. If egress is a blocker, Dedicated or Private avoids public egress.
[00:06:36] Lara Gomez: Can we run a quick AB test? Say current ranker vs Redwood reranked results on a subset?
[00:06:40] Maya Patel: Absolutely — we can set up an A/B with traffic split in the Console and capture evaluation metrics. Ethan will send instructions.
[00:06:48] Ethan Cole: I'll include an eval harness and a short script to compute NDCG.
[00:06:52] Priya Reddy: Anything about model version drift monitoring?
[00:06:56] Ethan Cole: Yes, the Console's quality monitoring ties to eval sets and can trigger regression alerts. Also Optimize suggests moving to quantized variants if latency spikes.
[00:07:07] Lara Gomez: We mentioned Pinecone earlier — how native is the integration?
[00:07:10] Maya Patel: It's a built-in connector; you can also use S3 dumps for bulk loads. I'll share connector docs link in the follow-up.
[00:07:18] Tom Ibrahim: Ok great — last thing, do you support deterministic rerank for auditing?
[00:07:22] Ethan Cole: We can provide cryptographic logging of model inputs/outputs and the audit trail, plus model pins for reproducibility. For strict auditing we usually recommend Private deploys.
[00:07:34] Lara Gomez: Nice. Any pricing red flags we should watch?
[00:07:37] Maya Patel: Main levers: candidate count, embedding model size, rerank model size, and query volume. Optimize will give recommended knobs. We'll send a pilot pricing estimate.
[00:07:48] Priya Reddy: Perfect.
[00:07:50] [00:08:00] (wrap up chatter)
[00:08:05] Maya Patel: Quick recap: Redwood will send hosted pricing and sample benchmarks; Ethan sends runbook + eval harness; Meridian will provide 10k doc sample and baseline metrics. We tentatively target a pilot kickoff next week pending materials.
[00:08:20] Lara Gomez: Yep we'll aim to send artifacts by Friday. Thanks Maya and Ethan.
[00:08:25] Maya Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the email and links to the Console sandbox, compliance pack, and code repo.
[00:08:32] (meeting ends)
